## SuperSubtitler 0.3.1 — speaker recognition, measured and tuned

Download both files into one folder: `SuperSubtitlerGUI.exe` (the window) and `SuperSubtitler.exe` (the engine).

### 🗨️ Speaker changes: four times fewer mistakes
- “Mark speaker changes” (`-speakers`) is now **measured**: a new test runs it on 66 minutes of hand-labelled debates and news with 1 to 11 speakers (VoxConverse) and scores every result.
- Six speaker models at many settings were compared. The winner, **3D-Speaker ERes2Net** at `speaker_threshold` 0.95, gets it wrong **10.8 %** of the time — 0.3.0's model at 0.5 got **44 %**, mostly by splitting one person into several (which meant “- ” lines where only one person spoke).
- The new model (26 MB) is downloaded once, pinned and checked like everything else, from the project's own mirror first.
- If your settings still hold 0.3.0's default (`speaker_threshold=0.50`), it is moved to the new default automatically; a value you chose yourself stays. The Settings page shows the new recommended range (0.85–1.05).
- CI now checks the error rate on every change to the speaker recognition, so it cannot quietly get worse.

The exes are not code-signed; Windows SmartScreen may warn — "More info" → "Run anyway". Built by GitHub Actions.
